/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_149_001-090_notes.md:435:“Le composé de (16)” only needs the natural map to the inverse limit of finite-level $H^1$ groups and compatibility with the Kummer maps; proving that this comparison is an isomorphism is unnecessary for the asserted injectivity. `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 073, repeats an inverse-limit identification in the multiplicative case, but its stronger-looking shorthand should not be imported as an unexamined exactness claim for every semiabelian group. The proof can avoid a separate derived-limit issue by showing that any element killed by the original Kummer map lies in every $nG(K)$.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_149_001-090_notes.md:459:The equivalence “si ce torseur est trivial -- i.e. si $\forall n$, $x$ se remonte” needs compatible lifts, not merely separate division points, but the missing compatibility follows here because the rational fibers of each finite multiplication map are finite and any finite family of conditions is dominated by one common multiple. Compactness of the resulting inverse system gives a coherent lift, while in characteristic $p$ the finite flat tower must not be called an étale covering tower when $p\mid n$. `LM_140-4_text.tex`, scans 169–170, repeats the inverse-isogeny viewpoint for one prime on $\mathbb G_m$ and differs by studying the arithmetic image, without supplying this all-$n$ compatibility argument.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_149_001-090_notes.md:722:**Confidence: high, because the absolute Frobenius supplies an explicit test of “1-fidèle.”** For $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb F_p$ and the reduced scheme $X=\mathbb A^1_S$, the distinct maps $t\mapsto t$ and $t\mapsto t^p$ induce naturally isomorphic morphisms of small étale topoi, as follows from the functorial relative-Frobenius isomorphism in the proof of the The Stacks Project Authors (2026, Tag 03SN). No direct Frobenius counterexample was located in the supplied context; the closest topos comparison, `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 171, distinguishes topoi without imposing this characteristic restriction, so the example adds a concrete reason for the manuscript's marginal question.

/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_149_001-090_notes.md:898:The proposed “forage de trous” should functorially construct $\Pi_{0,3}(I)$ of type $(0,3+\operatorname{card}I)$ from a finite Galois-stable set of admissible points. /workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_149_001-090_notes.md:906:**Confidence: high, because the finite-cover categories distinguish the two constructions.** The “sphère arithmétique” identified with $E_{Q(T_1)}$ must retain the inverse system over all finite puncture sets; actually filling all punctures and taking the usual fundamental group of $\mathbb P^1_Q$ yields only $G_Q$, since Riemann–Hurwitz excludes nontrivial connected geometric finite étale covers of $\mathbb P^1$ in characteristic zero. This adds a useful order-of-operations check to the equivariant filling formalism in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scans 175–179, and prevents conflating the function-field Galois group with the fundamental group of the unpunctured projective line.

Confidence: high, because polynomial Artin–Schreier classes detect the failure explicitly; this is an application of a known obstruction to the manuscript's wording, not a claim of a new counterexample in the literature.

Therefore (21), combined with the asserted free action on Hom sets of a nonempty groupoid, forces the acting total group E itself to be abelian, a stronger restriction than the centrality of π⊂E allowed in 093. The construction is consistent with 096’s legitimate covering-group example, but a genuinely noncommutative extension would require an inner-action/band formulation rather than this faithful constant Aut(id)-action. LM_140-3 scans 601 and 608 provide a concrete central noncommutative extension against which that restriction can be tested.

/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_003-047_notes.md:397:**Note:** For a geometric curve $C$ of graph type $G$, there is an exact sequence $1\to\prod_\alpha\operatorname{Aut}(Y_\alpha,\widehat I_\alpha)\to\operatorname{Aut}(C,I)\to\Gamma_C\to1$, where $\Gamma_C$ is the subgroup of graph automorphisms preserving the isomorphism class of the decorated collection of components. The subgroup $\Gamma_C$ can be smaller than Γ: gluing two nonisomorphic pointed elliptic curves at their origins gives a genus-two curve whose graph allows exchange of its two vertices, while the curve itself does not. The quotient presentation therefore does not assert that every curve's automorphism group contains the entire graph automorphism group, or that the extension splits.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_003-047_notes.md:485:**Note:** For a graph whose vertices all have genus zero and exactly three total special points, every factor of the pinned product is $\mathcal M_{0,\widehat I_\alpha}\simeq\mathcal M^!_{0,3}\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$, so its unpinned stratum is $B\operatorname{Aut}(G)$. /workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_149_091-136_notes.md:117:The expectation “être connu sur $H_1$” invites the following editorial counterexample: join two elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$ at rational points and smooth their single node over $\mathbf Q[[t]]$, locally by $xy=t$. /workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_149_091-136_notes.md:115:### RN100-03 — A separating node invisible to the Jacobian [own idea; scan 100, lower-left diagonal margin; compare scan 102 c)–d) and scan 103, manuscript p. 51, opening lines]
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_149_091-136_notes.md:117:The expectation “être connu sur $H_1$” invites the following editorial counterexample: join two elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$ at rational points and smooth their single node over $\mathbf Q[[t]]$, locally by $xy=t$. This adds a reduction test to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12, whose formula $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ separates the component genera from cycles in the dual graph. The graph is a tree, so the degree-zero Picard scheme has no toric part and the Jacobian has good reduction, whereas uniqueness of the stable model leaves the genus-two curve with its singular special fiber; its inertia on $H_1$ is therefore trivial despite bad curve reduction (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.11, Lemma 1.17, and Theorem 2.5; Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé X, Corollary 3.9). Confidence is high because independent node smoothing, the graph–torus computation, and stable-model uniqueness give each step; removing one section through a smooth rational point leaves $H_1$ unchanged and gives an affine hyperbolic counterexample as well.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_149_091-136_notes.md:133:The phrase “structure à l’infini” connects the action problem to the marked dual graph of a stable degeneration. This restates the “maquette” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 11, and adds an arithmetic question to the three boundary partitions of the four-pointed line on scan 61. Independent node-smoothing parameters give local boundary directions, while the graph distinguishes a separating node from a loop contributing to the Jacobian’s toric part (Deligne & Mumford, 1969, Proposition 1.5 and Lemma 1.17). Consequently the graph supplies useful test cases for the conjectural equivalences without itself determining the entire arithmetic outer action.

/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_142_001-093_notes.md:1693:For a complex scheme locally of finite type, analytification gives an equivalence between finite étale algebraic covers and finite topological covers, which yields (3) after fixing the corresponding geometric/analytic base point (Grothendieck, 1971/2003, Exposé XII, Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.2). /workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:172:The displayed “$\Pi_1 X^{*\infty}\simeq\operatorname{Lim}(\widetilde\Pi_1\leftarrow\widetilde\Pi_{2,1}\rightarrow\widetilde\Pi_2)$” claims that the complete flag system can be replaced, for this invariant, by the incidence cospan of codimensions one and two. It **adds** this collapse to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 131 and 133, which distinguish the partially functorial ordinary stratum groupoids from the proposed semisimplicial system of punctured-normal groupoids. A complete proof must specify the colimit convention and the comparison functor, then show that removing the higher strata and replacing the surviving diagram preserve the relevant fundamental groupoid; the objectwise descriptions of the $\widetilde\Pi$'s do not by themselves establish that conclusion. The formula targets the boundary $V^*_{\Theta,X}$, and scan 156 explicitly explains why such a formula can contain no ambient-space reconstruction in the curve case.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:184:The canceled, unfinished “Supposons que … $D_i^{*\infty}\leftrightarrow1$” begins a condition on the boundary structures and then selects an open-and-closed submultiplicity $D'_i$, but never supplies a conclusion. It **adds** an abandoned possible simplification to the punctured-torsor framework in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 123 and 130, where nontrivial torus fibers and the possible contribution of $\pi_2$ already obstruct an indiscriminate replacement of the data by points. The exact intended strength of the displayed relation with $1$, the scope of the index condition, and the role of the partially legible insertion remain reading questions; this is not a surviving corollary about contractibility. The later $K(\pi,1)$ expectation and its correction on scans 179–180 concern a different, explicitly discussed hypothesis and do not complete the deleted sentence.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:226:### 151-18 — Scan 156 — MPL_147_138-190_scan156.tex, lines 5–10 and 13–18, (254) — unpursued implication
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:256:The remark that normal crossings “ne joue plus de rôle depuis belle lurette” needs a specified scope when $X$ is replaced by a possibly singular admissible $\Sigma''$. It **differs** from `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 126 and 133, which expressly assign a nonformal role to normal-crossing neighborhood geometry in constructing the complete generization system. Current scans 189–190 later isolate global finite étaleness, manifold strata, and Boolean branch incidence as special properties, while reserving local triviality for tubular constructions. Read as a statement about the formal incidence category, the remark has a narrower plausible meaning; read as preserving every geometric property of the earlier construction under restriction, it remains unsupported by the passages cited.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:326:The statement “peut se décrire comme un produit fibré” proposes the defining square for the partially punctured neighborhood topos. This **adds** a nonformal neighborhood operation to `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 132–133, which carefully separates finite-cover base changes from the additional structure requiring normal crossings. A proof needs a site or germ construction for both neighborhood objects, a well-defined map induced by $A\subset B$, and a base-change theorem identifying the pullback with partial puncturing. Checking the square in a polydisc is necessary, but it does not by itself establish the global equivalence of topoi.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:340:### 164-13 — Scans 169 and 171; `MPL_147_138-190_scan169.tex`, lines 15–16 and 33–35, and `MPL_147_138-190_scan171.tex`, lines 36–40, (277), (281) — reading question — The two intermediate-stratum labels exchange places
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:350:The observation that the “nouveaux” elementary topoi first occur in (281) identifies a specific role for $\mathbb D\times\mathbb D^*$ and $\mathbb D^*\times\mathbb D$. It **adds** partially punctured neighborhood pieces to the intersection/flag combinatorics in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 106 and 113. The full nine-object product of the two three-object gluing spans records these mixed overlaps as well as $\mathbb D^*\times\mathbb D^*$, whereas the diagram for the complement of the origin omits the final bidisc piece. Thus a proposed minimal system of building blocks must justify any omission of a mixed piece by an explicit reconstruction, not merely by agreement of the separate strata.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:370:The “filtration canonique” labels $\check N_{d_*,d_i}$ with rank $d_i$, but (283) identifies it with a bundle for the immersion $D_{d_*}\to D_{d_i}$. This **differs** from `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 120 and 135–136, where the immersion into the codimension-$d_i$ stratum has codimension $d_0-d_i$. In particular, the rank-zero endpoint at index $0$ and the displayed definition of the top term cannot both be read as the standard relative normal bundle without an additional convention or a notational revision. The notes should preserve the conflict and test the two possible index conventions separately, rather than selecting one because it makes later formulas work.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:372:### 164-21 — Scans 173–174; `MPL_147_138-190_scan173.tex`, lines 3–5 and 39–48, and `MPL_147_138-190_scan174.tex`, lines 25–34 — unproved claim — Descent from local immersions to flag-space bundles
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:374:The phrase “immersion locale” matters because the flag spaces need not be globally embedded subspaces of their targets. This **restates** the local-immersion and finite-étale factorization in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 108, 128, and 136, but **adds** bundles and exact-sequence identifications on those flags. After settling the notation, a proof can construct the usual regular-immersion bundles in branch charts and then verify that their canonical transition maps descend through the finite étale flag covers; the scheme-theoretic local algebra is recorded in Stacks Project Authors (2026c, Lemma 31.22.6). The missing part is compatibility of that descent with every flag-forgetting morphism, not merely local exactness in one coordinate chart.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:418:One possible comparison is between the angular part of the punctured normal-line torsors and the torus fibers of the Kato–Nakayama space of the divisorial log structure. This **adds** a modern interpretation to the branch lattice and torsor in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 121–123, without asserting that Grothendieck has defined a log space on these pages. Talpo and Vistoli (2018, §3, especially the opening description and §§3.1–3.3) describe the real torus fibers and the normal-crossing real oriented blowup, providing a precise comparison target. **Confidence: medium** because the coordinate angular models agree, but an identification of the mixed flag neighborhoods would still require compatible restriction maps, descent through branch permutations, and a comparison of the relevant topoi.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:526:The “structure produit” in e) includes transverse strata, a distinguished point, and a simultaneous connected-neighbourhood condition, while the final NB says it has not yet been used. It **adds** a proposed topological substitute for the transverse analytic hypotheses of `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 120–121, and for the normal-crossing condition singled out as nonformal in scans 126 and 133. A proof should state the precise chart domain, the compatibility with closures, and what uniformity is intended along a stratum, then audit the intervening claims to ensure that local product triviality has not been assumed implicitly. This condition alone is not the conical stratification hypothesis checked in note 180-04.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:598:The fraction-like mark retained as uncertain $\tfrac12$ before “simplicial” should not be interpreted as a modern categorical truncation without further evidence. It **restates** the notation “$1/2$-simplicial” in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scans 128 and 133–134, where maps of ordered simplices and degeneracies are both discussed. Segal (1968, §§1–2) likewise uses “semi-simplicial” for a convention including degeneracies, so historical terminology supports a question about the abbreviation rather than a decision to erase degeneracy maps. The visible sign and the author's actual indexing conventions remain authoritative for the diplomatic text.

/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_147_138-190_notes.md:628:The “premier sommet” projection is asserted finite étale over $D^*_{\Delta_0}$, with strict flags its inverse image, and the normal-crossing case is asserted finite étale over the whole base. This **restates** the strict inverse-image relation in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 129, and **generalizes** its finite flag-cover description in scans 128 and 132, which uses the finite branch set and first-vertex-preserving maps. A proof must separate finiteness of a fibre from local constancy of the family, and identify how the frontier and connected-germ conditions give a stable incidence set as the origin moves along an intrinsic stratum. The final claim that e) remains unused makes it especially useful to check this argument without importing local product charts.

/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/LM_140-2_notes.md:1900:**S07. Scans 128 and 130. Implication not pursued [second pass].** The "calcul habituel … que j'ai un peu oublié" can be written down in the case used on scan 130. The local situation $B_{D,D^{*}}$ is $B_{X,U}$ with (D, D*) in place of (X, U), so its recollement gives a long exact sequence $\cdots\to H^q_{s_i}\to H^q(\Gamma_i,\cdot)\to H^q(\mathcal E_i,\cdot)\to H^{q+1}_{s_i}\to\cdots$. Over an algebraically closed k, $\Gamma_i=1$ and $\mathcal E_i=\Pi_i$. With coefficients $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ (as a limit over $\mathbb Z/n$) this gives $H^2_{s_i}\simeq H^1(\Pi_i,\widehat{\mathbb Z})=\operatorname{Hom}(\Pi_i,\widehat{\mathbb Z})$. That is $L_i^{\otimes-1}$ once $\Pi_i$ is identified with $L_i$, which is the displayed isomorphism "$H^2_{s_i}(B_{U,X},\widehat{\mathbb Z})\simeq L_i^{\otimes-1}$".

/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/LM_140-2_notes.md:6670:B. **Scans 545 and 547, freeness of $\Gamma'_{2m,2}$ and the gerbe. Claim checked (second pass).** Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $\ne2$, the kernel of $\operatorname{Aut}(E)\to\operatorname{GL}(E[2])$ is $\{\pm1\}$. /workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_142_001-093_notes.md:1769:### N070.3 — The abelianized path correction gives a computable Kummer test
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_142_001-093_notes.md:1774:For \(x,y\in K^\times\), lift the path normalized from 1 to \(y/x\) through \(z\mapsto z^n\), obtaining compatible roots \(\alpha_n^n=y/x\); the image of its correction at level n is \(u(\alpha_n)/\alpha_n\), representing the Kummer class of \(y/x\). For \(X=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\), the two maps \(z\) and \(1-z\) give the two abelianized classes of \(y/x\) and \((1-y)/(1-x)\), with the chosen loop conventions fixing their signs. /workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_149_091-136_notes.md:29:The phrase “seul le facteur $I_{s^{\prime}}\simeq T$” isolates the inertia left before a residual section can be chosen. For an equicharacteristic-zero henselian trait, a uniformizer supplies a splitting, and its inertia-conjugacy classes form a torsor under $H^1(k,\widehat{\mathbf Z}(1))\simeq\varprojlim_n k^\times/(k^\times)^n$ (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 03PK). /workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/LM_OVERVIEW.md:62:[I] Four contacts, each handled by one prompt on each side (README, "Overlaps"): the Teichmüller tower and the stratification of `M̄_{0,n}`; multi-Galois topoi and locally constant coefficients; gluing along an open and its closed complement (hole-filling here, collages and links there); levels of faithfulness ("3-fidèle" here, the three-level criterion for 1-types there). [H] The common root is that in both manuscripts he refuses a base point and a single invariant, and works with the whole system of objects and the operations between them; in 1981 the system is a tower of profinite groups with outer actions, in 1990 a family of categories of coefficients with Kan extensions. The 1981 text has the arithmetic and no homotopy theory above level 2; the 1990 text has all levels and no arithmetic. /workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_146_001-099_notes.md:1492:The margin "l’extension est ici néc. centrale" follows from naturality: a constant π-action through Aut(id) commutes with every automorphism at each object. /workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_142_001-093_notes.md:429:The stated justification is too broad in characteristic \(p>0\): Artin–Schreier covers of \(\mathbb A^1\) acquire new coefficients after extending an algebraically closed field, so the canonical base-change map on full étale fundamental groups need not be an isomorphism (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0A47). The category-level equivalence asserted here therefore needs its own hypotheses and cannot follow from the unqualified fundamental-group sentence.
/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/MPL_142_001-093_notes.md:449:On a category containing the actual curves and their base changes, field automorphisms act functorially by transport of coefficients. If one then replaces the objects by one representative for each numerical type, the identifications with those representatives require choices of paths or isomorphisms, and the transported action must be tracked with its coherence isomorphisms. At a single chosen object, this is the familiar distinction between an action on a groupoid and an outer action on its fundamental group.

/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/LM_140-2_notes.md:1900:**S07. Scans 128 and 130. Implication not pursued [second pass].** The "calcul habituel … que j'ai un peu oublié" can be written down in the case used on scan 130. The local situation $B_{D,D^{*}}$ is $B_{X,U}$ with (D, D*) in place of (X, U), so its recollement gives a long exact sequence $\cdots\to H^q_{s_i}\to H^q(\Gamma_i,\cdot)\to H^q(\mathcal E_i,\cdot)\to H^{q+1}_{s_i}\to\cdots$. Over an algebraically closed k, $\Gamma_i=1$ and $\mathcal E_i=\Pi_i$. With coefficients $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ (as a limit over $\mathbb Z/n$) this gives $H^2_{s_i}\simeq H^1(\Pi_i,\widehat{\mathbb Z})=\operatorname{Hom}(\Pi_i,\widehat{\mathbb Z})$. That is $L_i^{\otimes-1}$ once $\Pi_i$ is identified with $L_i$, which is the displayed isomorphism "$H^2_{s_i}(B_{U,X},\widehat{\mathbb Z})\simeq L_i^{\otimes-1}$".

/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/LM_140-2_notes.md:6248:**G. Scan 507 · claim without proof (verified).** In the anharmonic group, the stabiliser of 0 is $\{x,\ x/(x-1)\}$, that of −1 is $\{x,\ 1/x\}$, and that of −j is generated by $x\mapsto 1/(1-x)$, whose fixed points are the roots of $x^2-x+1$, namely $-j$ and $-\bar j$. The orbits $\{0,1,\infty\}$, $\{-1,\tfrac12,2\}$, $\{-j,-\bar j\}$ thus have ramification indices 2, 2, 3 over $a_0,a_1,a_\infty$, as the text says. This also confirms the minus signs (the witnesses' $\{j,\bar j\}$ is wrong). The normalised quotient is $f(x)=27x^2(x-1)^2/\bigl(4(x^2-x+1)^3\bigr)=1728/j(x)$, with $j(x)=256(x^2-x+1)^3/(x^2(x-1)^2)$ the Legendre j-invariant. It has double zeros at 0, 1, ∞, triple poles at $-j,-\bar j$, and $f-1=-(x+1)^2(2x-1)^2(x-2)^2/\bigl(4(x^2-x+1)^3\bigr)$.

/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/LM_140-2_notes.md:6478:**S09, scan 529, lower margin, conjecture answered (mine; confidence high for the group theory).** Conjugation by S fixes ε and swaps β, κ; conjugation by T sends ε ↦ εκ, β ↦ βκ, κ ↦ κ. So 𝔖₃ = Sl(2,ℤ)/Γ(2) permutes the four complements with orbits {Ker εβκ} and {Ker ε, Ker εβ, Ker εκ}: exactly one complement is normal in Sl(2,ℤ). The Legendre image Ker ε is not normal, so "je présume que oui" holds for one of the four lifts only (with R31's matrices, the twist by λ(1−λ)). For that one, Sl(2,ℤ)/Ker εβκ has order 12 and S has order 4 in it (S² = −1 ∉ Ker εβκ), so it is the dicyclic group ℤ/3 ⋊ ℤ/4, a non-split central extension of 𝔖₃ by ±1.

/workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/LM_140-3_notes.md:422:32. **Scan 39, §40 and (49) — unproved claim — correct.** The heading is "Paraphrase topologico-isotopique (en termes des groupes fondamentaux) de la Théorie de Legendre", not "Reformulation", and the group in (49) is 𝔖₀,₃. /workspace/scratch/d461dfc25ad4/context/SECTIONS_STATE.md:80:**Grothendieck's state; published versions.** The letter to Tate (Pisa, May 1966) is the founding text of crystalline cohomology: it names crystals and conjectures that de Rham cohomology is a crystal [V: Illusie quotes it]. Grothendieck developed it in IHES lectures in November–December 1966, published as "Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes" (notes by Coates and Jussila) in *Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas* (1968; Circle copy https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~leila.schneps/grothendieckcircle/DixExp.pdf) [V reference; link checked]. Barsotti–Tate groups: ICM Nice 1970, "Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux" (https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~leila.schneps/grothendieckcircle/GroupesB-T.pdf) and the Montréal lectures, *Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné*, SMS 45 (1974) [V reference in Illusie]. His letter to Illusie of 2–4 December 1969 on deformations of Barsotti–Tate groups was written up by Illusie, "Déformations de groupes de Barsotti-Tate, d'après A.
